intent_record.what: A new static __always_inline helper function named is_user_task(struct task_struct *task) was added, returning true when task->mm is non-NULL and the task flags do not include PF_KTHREAD or PF_USER_WORKER.
intent_record.how: This introduces a reusable runtime predicate for identifying normal user tasks while excluding kernel threads and user worker tasks, enabling callers to consistently distinguish user tasks based on memory context and task flags.

consistency_review.core_intent: Replace ad hoc user-task eligibility checks in perf callchain handling with the canonical `is_user_task(current)` classification so user register and user-memory callchain collection only occurs for actual user tasks.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability was caused by relying only on PF_KTHREAD/PF_USER_WORKER to infer a task was safe for user-space profiling even when mm could be NULL during exit. This change directly addresses that by adding a helper that also requires a valid mm while excluding those flags.

The root cause was perf using PF_KTHREAD/PF_USER_WORKER-style task checks to decide user profiling safety, which could misclassify exiting tasks with current->mm == NULL. This group directly replaces those ad hoc checks with the canonical is_user_task(current) logic in perf user-register and user-callchain collection paths, addressing that misclassification.

candidates.rationale: This is the core flawed classification logic: it treats a task as eligible for user callchain handling solely by negating PF_KTHREAD/PF_USER_WORKER, without verifying current->mm is still valid during exit.

This check is the direct buggy gate before falling through to task_pt_regs(current) for user register retrieval; it only excludes flagged kernel/user-worker tasks and misses exiting tasks with NULL mm.
This branch decides whether perf may collect user registers from a non-user-mode context using only task flags, which is exactly the root cause described.
This statement guards the user-page lookup path with the same insufficient flag-only test, allowing access to user-memory state when current->mm may already be NULL.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the core vulnerable classification expression in perf_callchain(): it decides user-space profiling eligibility solely by checking PF_KTHREAD/PF_USER_WORKER flags. That misses the task-exit case where a task is still not marked as a kernel thread/worker but current->mm is already NULL, leading perf to treat it as a user task and later dereference invalid user-state.

This branch permits collection of user registers from a non-user-mode context based only on PF_KTHREAD/PF_USER_WORKER. Because it does not verify that the task is still a valid user task with a live mm, it can execute during task exit and contribute to dereferencing user state after current->mm became NULL.

This guard controls the user-page lookup path using the same insufficient flag-only logic. It allows perf to proceed on tasks that are no longer safe for user profiling during exit, when current->mm may already be NULL.

This gate rejects only kernel threads and user workers before falling through to user register retrieval. By relying exclusively on flags, it incorrectly treats exiting tasks with NULL mm as safe user tasks, enabling the later bad dereference while collecting user callchain state.
